claim_verdicts.evidence: Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). Definition of the vocab term disaster-recovery as the course uses it (outline item 1, verbatim). No behaviour, number or syntax; no pinned source in versions.yaml defines DR, and the lesson does not attribute the wording to one.

NIST CSRC Glossary, RPO: "The point in time to which data must be recovered after an outage." (source SP 800-34 Rev. 1) - supports the RPO half. RTO: "The overall length of time an information system's components can be in the recovery phase before negatively impacting the organization's mission or mission/business processes." The ledger's 'after a failure until it works again' anchors the period at the failure; the source anchors it to the recovery phase and limits it by harm to the mission. Body's 'how long the business accepts ... unusable' fits; ledger wording should follow the source.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: RPO is the point in time to which data must be recovered after an outage, so data written after it may be lost; the lesson counts it as time before the failure. RTO is the overall time the system may spend in recovery, unusable, before the outage harms the business.

claim_verdicts.evidence: NIST CSRC Glossary, RTO: "The overall length of time an information system's components can be in the recovery phase before negatively impacting the organization's mission or mission/business processes." 'Overall' supports 'not only the restore command'. The glossary does not say when the period starts or whether detection is in it; it says 'recovery phase', undefined there. csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/recovery_phase and .../activation_notification_phase return 404. 'From the failure' and 'detection' stay without evidence. Not contradicted.

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). PostgreSQL 17 pg_dump: "Dumps can be output in script or archive file formats. Script dumps are plain-text files containing the SQL commands required to reconstruct the database"; -F p plain: "Output a plain-text SQL script file (the default)."; -s: "Dump only the object definitions (schema), not data." The new definition states the default script format as what pg_dump always writes.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `pg_dump` is PostgreSQL's tool that writes a database out as a file, called a dump; by default, as here, the file is plain SQL statements that rebuild the database.

issues.text: New in round 2 (added definition). pg_dump also writes archive formats (custom, directory, tar) restored with pg_restore; 'a file of SQL statements' is only the default plain format, which this script uses. The ledger claim 7 repeats the over-general wording.

issues.text: Claim 3 (RTO clock starts at the failure and includes noticing it) is unverified against the new key dr_glossary: the NIST glossary defines RTO as time 'in the recovery phase' and does not say whether detection is part of it. §4, §6 misconception 2 and quiz explanations (lines 47, 224, 226: 'the clock starts at the failure') rest on that reading. Fact kind, so not blocking.
issues.quote: On the right, the clock starts when the failure happens and stops when customers can order again.
issues.fix: No body change required now. Owner: mirror NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 (§3.2.1, phases) into refs/web so the start of the RTO period can be checked; if it places detection outside the recovery phase, reword §4 to 'the RTO bounds the overall recovery, from the moment recovery has to start until customers can order again' and adjust the quiz explanations.
